Coinbase to Automatically Convert 14 Restricted Crypto Assets for EEA Users on October 30 Under Coinbase's previously announced MiCA compliance measures, retail users in the European Economic Area (EEA) must withdraw 14 restricted crypto assets, including USDT, PYUSD, USD1, DAI, and PAXG, before October 30. On that date, Coinbase will automatically convert remaining balances into USDC or other supported assets or currencies at prevailing market rates. Trading and conversions of these assets have already been restricted. Coinbase warned that deposits received after the deadline will not be credited to user accounts or included in the automatic conversion process, and recovery cannot be guaranteed. The restrictions affect assets issued by Tether, PayPal, and Trump-linked World Liberty Financial, among others. — link

Reuters: CFTC Again Probes Whether Polymarket Violated 2022 Settlement According to Reuters, citing two sources familiar with the matter, the CFTC is investigating whether Polymarket violated its 2022 settlement by failing to take sufficient steps to block U.S. users from its offshore platform. The investigation covers Polymarket's geolocation controls and U.S. advertising activities. The agency is also examining customer onboarding and protection measures on Polymarket's U.S. platform. The CFTC and DOJ closed similar investigations in 2025 without bringing charges. Both Polymarket and the CFTC declined to comment. — link

Wallet Potentially Linked to $40M UXLINK Hack Shows $6.54M in Unrealized ETH Gains A wallet suspected of belonging to the hacker behind last year’s roughly $40 million UXLINK theft holds a 30,282 ETH long on Hyperliquid, according to on-chain data. The position has an average entry price of $2,134.45 and is worth approximately $71.17 million, with $6.54 million in unrealized gains. A funding address associated with the position and a known UXLINK hacker address both transferred ETH held for gas fees to the same wallet on the same day. The trader began trading ETH on Hyperliquid in early August after consolidating roughly 11.55 million USDC from multiple sources, with five of six trades showing a profit. — link

Robinhood Q3 Revenue Meets Estimates as Prediction Market Revenue Surges and Crypto Revenue Falls 55% Robinhood reported Q3 2026 revenue of $1.424 billion, up 12% year-over-year and roughly in line with the $1.42 billion estimate. Net income fell 14% to $476 million, while diluted EPS of $0.51 missed the $0.56 estimate, including $0.07 per share in unrealized losses primarily related to Robinhood Ventures Fund I. Adjusted EBITDA rose 9% to $808 million. Prediction market event contract revenue increased more than sixfold to $173 million, while crypto transaction revenue declined 55% to $120 million. Crypto notional trading volume fell 38% to $50 billion, while event contracts traded rose more than sevenfold to 16.4 billion. Robinhood Chain recorded over $80 billion in DEX trading volume and more than $50 million in network fees during its first quarter on mainnet. The company also lowered the upper end of its 2026 adjusted operating expenses and stock-based compensation outlook from $2.775 billion to $2.75 billion, keeping the lower end at $2.675 billion. — link
